findings.title: CSRF protection disabled on OData backend routes
findings.issue: Both `/odata/v4/CatalogService` and `/sap/*` approuter routes declare `csrfProtection: false`. These destinations are reached by authenticated POST/PATCH calls from the UI (lock Acquire/Release/Heartbeat, child contract create/update). Disabling CSRF makes those write operations vulnerable to cross-site request forgery when the user has an active xsuaa session.
findings.severityRationale: Write endpoints behind an xsuaa-authenticated session are exposed without CSRF protection — a classic high-impact vulnerability with a concrete exploit path.
findings.recommendation: Remove `csrfProtection: false` (default is true) on both routes. The UI already fetches X-CSRF-Token tokens before POST/PATCH; the approuter should forward and validate them.

findings.title: No scopes or role templates defined — application is effectively unauthorized
findings.issue: `xs-security.json` declares empty `scopes` and `role-templates`. The approuter protects routes with `authenticationType: xsuaa`, but any authenticated user can reach the OData endpoints because no fine-grained scope (e.g. `$XSAPPNAME.ContractEditor`) is enforced. The FD states 'One custom role is required' — this is not implemented.
findings.severityRationale: Missing authorization model on a procurement app that mutates purchase contracts — a direct business-rule failure and a security gap.
findings.recommendation: Declare a scope (e.g. `ContractDisplay`, `ContractEditor`), bind it to a role template, and enforce it on `/odata/*` and `/sap/*` routes via `scope` in `xs-app.json`. Mirror the role in CAP `@requires` annotations.

findings.title: `attachRouteMatched` registered inside `_onRouteMatched` — handler count grows on each navigation
findings.issue: `_onRouteMatched` runs every time the user navigates to the child contract page. It registers a new `oRouter.attachRouteMatched(fn)` listener each time, with no corresponding detach. After N navigations there are N listeners firing concurrently, each closing over a stale `this._sCurrentParentContract`, which can release the wrong lock and corrupt view state.
findings.severityRationale: Accumulating listeners that mutate shared router/lock state produce real race conditions and spurious lock-release calls in production.
findings.recommendation: Register the router handler ONCE in `onInit` (or use `attachRoutePatternMatched` on a specific route), store the handler reference, and `detachRouteMatched` in `onExit`.

findings.title: `onExit` missing — lock polling, heartbeat, and backup objects leak on controller destroy
findings.issue: The controller creates `setInterval` handles (`_iLockPollInterval`, `_iHeartbeatInterval`), a `window.onbeforeunload` listener, and heavy JSON models, but there is no `onExit`. When the view is destroyed by router navigation, intervals keep firing against a destroyed view, which also keeps the server lock held until TTL expires.
findings.severityRationale: Live intervals continue to call `_checkLockStatus` and `_sendHeartbeat` after destruction — users will be locked out of contracts they already left, and background requests persist indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Implement `onExit() { this._stopLockPolling(); this._stopHeartbeat(); this._releaseLock(this._sCurrentParentContract); window.onbeforeunload = null; }` and detach any router listeners.
findings.codeSnippet: // controller declares intervals but has no onExit hook

findings.title: `window.onbeforeunload = fn` overwrites any existing handler and prevents stacking
findings.issue: Assigning directly to `window.onbeforeunload` replaces any other handler (host FLP shell, other open apps) and cannot be stacked. On tab close the handler runs — but it accesses `this.getView()`, which may already be in teardown.
findings.severityRationale: Replaces a shared browser global; the FLP shell relies on this hook for its own unsaved-changes dialog.
findings.recommendation: Use `window.addEventListener('beforeunload', fn)` plus a corresponding `removeEventListener` in `onExit`.

findings.title: N+1 OData reads: one request per child row to fetch Plant
findings.issue: `_fetchPlantsForChildren` loops over every child context and issues a separate `oModel.read('/A_PurchaseContract(X)')` with `$expand=to_PurchaseContractItem`. For N child contracts this triggers N round-trips. The Plant could be requested with the parent contract list in a single call via `$expand=to_PurchaseContractItem($select=Plant)` or via `$batch`.
findings.severityRationale: Scales linearly with the number of children — on a parent with 50 children, 50 serial OData calls block the UI.
findings.recommendation: Add `$expand=to_PurchaseContractItem` on the initial list binding or group reads with `oModel.submitChanges({ groupId })` / `$batch` and request all plants in one go.

findings.title: Direct `jQuery.$.ajax` to OData service instead of the ODataModel API
findings.issue: Child creation (POST), target amount update (PATCH), and lock Acquire/Release/Heartbeat all bypass the registered ODataModel and call `$.ajax` with manually-fetched CSRF tokens. This duplicates CSRF handling, skips model-level caching and error aggregation, and does not integrate with `oModel.hasPendingChanges()` / draft handling.
findings.severityRationale: Hand-rolled HTTP on a model that already offers `create()` / `update()` / `callFunction()` creates divergent CSRF/token/error paths and makes future upgrades to OData v4 much harder.
findings.recommendation: Use `oModel.create(...)`, `oModel.update(...)` for OData v2 writes and `oModel.callFunction(...)` or action imports for AcquireLock/ReleaseLock/HeartbeatLock on CAP. Let the model manage CSRF.
findings.codeSnippet: $.ajax({ url: sUrl, method: "POST", headers: { "X-CSRF-Token": csrfToken }, data: JSON.stringify(oPayload), ... });

findings.title: `sap.ui.xmlfragment` is deprecated — use `Fragment.load`
findings.issue: `_onRouteMatched` and `onCreateChild` both instantiate the dialog with the deprecated factory `sap.ui.xmlfragment(id, name, controller)`. It is listed as deprecated since UI5 1.56 in favour of `Fragment.load({...})`.
findings.severityRationale: Deprecated factory flagged by the SAPUI5 SDK; the newer `Fragment.load` is already used elsewhere in the controller for `plantVH`, so this is inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Replace both calls with `Fragment.load({ id: ..., name: ..., controller: this }).then(oDlg => { this.getView().addDependent(oDlg); ... })`.

findings.title: `sap.ui.getCore().applyChanges()` is a deprecated synchronisation hack
findings.issue: `_saveChildAfterValidation` calls `sap.ui.getCore().applyChanges()` to force a synchronous render before issuing PATCH requests. The Core-level synchronous flush is deprecated and unreliable with async rendering (UI5 1.136+).
findings.severityRationale: Deprecated API that will be removed; the pattern also masks a real race between change event and binding update.
findings.recommendation: Rely on the `change` event of the Input (which already fires before `onSaveChild`) and remove the forced applyChanges. If needed, use `oInput.getBinding('value').updateValue()` on individual rows.

findings.title: Main business dataSource uses OData v2 — v4 preferred
findings.issue: `mainService` points at `/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_PURCHASECONTRACT_PROCESS_SRV;v=0002/` with `odataVersion: "2.0"`. The project already consumes `api_purchaseorder_2` via OData v4 — mixing v2 and v4 forces two bindings, two formatters, and two CSRF flows. SAP recommends OData v4 for new S/4HANA Cloud Fiori apps.
findings.severityRationale: Mixing OData versions is a maintainability smell; downgraded to Low per the universal rule but kept at Medium because the entire write path (create + patch + lock) is coupled to v2 semantics.
findings.recommendation: Switch `mainService` to the OData v4 variant of API_PURCHASECONTRACT_PROCESS and refactor controllers to use the v4 ODataModel bindings. Keep v2 only if v4 is unavailable for a specific scenario.

findings.title: `YY1_CORP_PLANT_F4_CDS` dataSource also uses OData v2
findings.issue: The plant value-help service `YY1_CORP_PLANT_F4_CDS` is declared as `odataVersion: "2.0"`. Fresh custom CDS value helps in S/4HANA Cloud ship with an OData v4 variant that integrates with the v4 `sap.ui.model.odata.v4.ODataModel`.
findings.severityRationale: OData v2 where v4 exists — universal check mandates Low.
findings.recommendation: Expose the plant F4 CDS as an OData v4 service binding (`srvb_odata_v4_api`) and update the model.

findings.title: `flexEnabled: false` disables Key User UI adaptation
findings.issue: The manifest sets `sap.ui5.flexEnabled: false`. For S/4HANA Public Cloud, Key User Adaptation at Runtime (RTA) is a core non-functional requirement — personalisation and in-app extensions rely on `flexEnabled: true`.
findings.severityRationale: Blocks the standard S/4HANA Cloud extensibility story; the FD explicitly places this on Public Cloud.
findings.recommendation: Set `flexEnabled: true` and ensure fragments carry stable IDs so RTA changes survive upgrades.

findings.title: Unbounded initial OData read on contract list in `onInit`
findings.issue: `onInit` binds the main table to `/A_PurchaseContract` with only a type filter (`PurchaseContractType = 'ZCP0'`). There is no `$top`, no `growingThreshold`, and the `sap.m.Table` in the view does not set `growing="true"`. On a tenant with thousands of ZCP0 contracts the first render will pull the entire set.
findings.severityRationale: Universal check: `onInit` loads must be bounded to 50–100 records and should prefer lazy loading.
findings.recommendation: Add `growing="true"` and `growingThreshold="50"` on the `<Table>` and limit the binding via `length: 50` or `threshold`. Make the user press 'More' or scroll to lazy-load.

findings.title: Child contract table has no paging / growing
findings.issue: `childContractTable` binds `purchasecontract>/A_PurchaseContract` with a filter but no `growing="true"`. The follow-up logic (plant fetch, residual calc) iterates ALL contexts, so an unbounded dataset means an unbounded chain of OData reads.
findings.severityRationale: Compounded by finding #6 — unbounded fan-out makes the N+1 explode.
findings.recommendation: Add `growing="true" growingThreshold="25"` on the table and run the per-row calculations lazily on `updateFinished`.

findings.title: Edit button no longer binds to lock model — concurrency guard is bypassed in UI
findings.issue: The commented-out block at lines 39–45 shows the intended `enabled="{= !${lock>/isLocked} || ${lock>/isMyLock} }"` binding. The active Button (lines 46–50) has no `enabled` binding, so even while another user holds the lock the Edit button is clickable. The controller does enforce the lock on the server, but the UI contract described in the lock-management section is broken.
findings.severityRationale: Users will click Edit, see 'Contract is locked by another user' pop-ups constantly, and in a race window may still modify local state (`_createChildBackup`) before the server rejects.
findings.recommendation: Remove the dead comment block and re-apply the `enabled` and `tooltip` bindings on the live Button. Keep the server-side lock check as defence in depth.

findings.title: Global `sap.ui.model.json.JSONModel` lookup instead of required module
findings.issue: Several places use the global namespace path (e.g. `new sap.ui.model.json.JSONModel(...)` at lines 44, 51; `sap.ui.model.Filter` at line 412; `sap.ui.core.Fragment.byId` at lines 255, 862; `sap.ui.core.routing.History.getInstance()` at 352; `sap.m.MessageBox`, `sap.m.MessageToast`, `sap.ui.getCore()`). Globals bypass the AMD dependency graph, inflate the preload bundle, and break tree-shaking.
findings.severityRationale: Bad practice flagged by UI5 best practices; mixed usage is confusing and error-prone.
findings.recommendation: Use the modules already listed in `sap.ui.define` (`JSONModel`, `Filter`, `Fragment`) consistently, and add missing dependencies (`History`, `MessageBox`, `MessageToast`) to the define block.

findings.title: `console.log` left in production controller
findings.issue: Several `console.log` / `console.warn` / `console.error` calls are left in the shipped controller (lines 48, 51, 230, 233, 844, 1087). These bypass `sap.base.Log` (which is already imported) and cannot be silenced via log level in production.
findings.severityRationale: Noise in the browser console, loss of log-level control, risk of PII leakage.
findings.recommendation: Replace every `console.*` with the already-imported `Log.info/debug/warn/error`. Delete pure debug prints.

findings.title: `sap.ushell.Container` accessed without require and without fallback for non-FLP preview
findings.issue: `sap.ushell.Container.getUser()` is wrapped in a `try/catch`, but during the `fiori run` preview flow `sap.ushell` is undefined, so `_sCurrentUserId` falls back to `'UNKNOWN'`. That value is then sent to `AcquireLock` as the lock owner — every developer runs will fight over the same `UNKNOWN` lock on the shared CAP backend.
findings.severityRationale: Guaranteed collision on dev/preview environments and a weak audit trail (anonymous locks).
findings.recommendation: During local run, generate a session-scoped pseudo user (e.g. `sess_<guid>`) instead of a static `UNKNOWN`. Guard the ushell access with a `sap.ui.require(['sap/ushell/Container'])` or `sap.ui.getCore().getLoadedLibraries().sap.ushell`.

findings.title: Hardcoded CAP service URL fallback
findings.issue: If the registered `CatalogService` model has no `sServiceUrl`, the controller falls back to the hardcoded path `/odata/v4/CatalogService`. Any approuter prefix change (multi-tenancy, versioning) will silently misroute every lock request.
findings.severityRationale: A silent misroute on a critical concurrency feature is a plausible operational failure.
findings.recommendation: Fail loudly (`Log.error`) if the model is not registered, and surface the lock feature as unavailable rather than guessing a path. Resolve URL exclusively from the manifest-registered model.

findings.title: `setTimeout(fn, 0)` used to patch dialog-field population timing
findings.issue: `onCreateChild` wraps the dialog field initialisation in `setTimeout(fn, 0)` to work around the race between `dialog.open()` and fragment field availability. This is a timing hack: on a slower machine the inputs may still be undefined when the timeout fires.
findings.severityRationale: Flaky UX; the correct hook is already available.
findings.recommendation: Populate values in the dialog's `afterOpen` event, or await `Fragment.load(...)` before calling `open()`.

findings.title: Child contract key constructed by naive string concatenation
findings.issue: `oPayload.PurchaseContract = sParentContract + sSapcode;` with no padding, no delimiter, and no uniqueness check. Two parents with `12345` + SAP code `01` and `1234` + SAP code `501` both resolve to `1234501`. The subsequent POST may succeed, overwrite the wrong contract, or trigger an opaque backend error.
findings.severityRationale: A deterministic collision path for duplicate keys in a procurement system is a hard business-rule failure.
findings.recommendation: Validate uniqueness via OData read before POST, or let the backend generate the key (RAP late numbering / draft) and inject SAP code into a dedicated custom field.

findings.title: Validation re-reads parent after already having its target locally
findings.issue: `validateAgainstParent` issues another `oParentModel.read('/A_PurchaseContract')` purely to retrieve `PurchaseContractTargetAmount`, which `_calculateParentResidual` already fetched and stored in the `parentInfo` model. On every Check click the UI makes a redundant OData call that competes with other requests.
findings.severityRationale: Unnecessary round-trip on every validation, and the two reads can diverge (parent changed between calls) producing inconsistent error messages.
findings.recommendation: Reuse `this.parentTarget` (already stored on the controller) or read from `parentInfo>/PurchaseContractTargetAmount_raw`.

findings.title: Parallel PATCH per child row without batch — partial-failure state is unclear
findings.issue: `_saveChildAfterValidation` fires one `$.ajax` PATCH per child context in parallel. On a partial failure (3 of 5 succeed) the UI reports a single generic `errorWhileSavingChildContracts` toast — the user cannot tell which rows actually saved, and the view model is not rolled back for the successful ones.
findings.severityRationale: Data integrity hazard: user believes save failed and retries, double-applying residual recalculation.
findings.recommendation: Group the PATCHes in a `$batch` (OData v2 `deferredGroups`) or `cds.tx` on the CAP side. On partial failure, report row-level diagnostics and either roll back successes or keep the view in edit mode with a clear per-row status indicator.

findings.title: Lock ownership trusts client-provided `UserId`
findings.issue: `AcquireLock` sends `UserId: this._sCurrentUserId` from the browser. If the CAP service also uses this payload field to decide the lock owner (instead of resolving the user from the request's JWT via `req.user.id`), a malicious client can impersonate any user to steal or release their lock.
findings.severityRationale: Classic broken-access-control pattern; feasible via browser dev tools against the live approuter route.
findings.recommendation: CAP service MUST resolve the lock owner from `req.user.id` and ignore the client-sent `UserId`. The field in the payload should be removed or treated as display-only.

findings.title: `$expand` with nested `$filter` executed per child contract
findings.issue: `_computeChildOrderedAndResidual` calls `oPOModel.bindList('/PurchaseOrder', ... { $filter: "PurchaseContract eq '...'", $expand: '_PurchaseOrderItem(...)' })` once per child row. The same information could be retrieved for all children in a single call via `$filter=PurchaseContract in ('A','B','C')`.
findings.severityRationale: Same N+1 pattern as #6, but on the purchase-order service; magnifies latency.
findings.recommendation: Collect all `PurchaseContract` keys first, then issue one list binding with `PurchaseContract in (...)`. Reduce or request contexts in a single `$batch`.
findings.codeSnippet:
var sFilter = "PurchaseContract eq '" + sChildContract + "'";
oListBinding = oPOModel.bindList("/PurchaseOrder", null, null, null, { $filter: sFilter, $expand: sExpand });

findings.title: `MessageBox` `title: "Error" / "Success"` is hardcoded
findings.issue: Multiple `MessageBox.error({..., title: 'Error'})` and `MessageBox.success({..., title: 'Success'})` leave the dialog title untranslated. The body text is correctly bound through i18n but the title defeats the i18n story for Italian/English toggle.
findings.severityRationale: Minor UX inconsistency; not a defect.
findings.recommendation: Add i18n keys `errorTitle=Error` / `successTitle=Success` (and `errorTitle=Errore` / `successTitle=Successo` in `i18n_it.properties`) and bind `title: oBundle.getText('errorTitle')`.

findings.title: User-facing fallback strings not translated
findings.issue: `_acquireLock` reject uses literal `'Contract is locked by another user.'` and `'Failed to acquire lock. Please try again.'` instead of i18n keys. Error paths bypass the resource bundle.
findings.severityRationale: Minor i18n hygiene gap on error paths.
findings.recommendation: Add resource bundle keys and resolve through `getResourceBundle().getText(...)` before `reject(...)`.
findings.codeSnippet: reject(oResult.Message || "Contract is locked by another user.");

findings.title: `try/catch` with empty handler swallows decode errors
findings.issue: `try { sParentContract = decodeURIComponent(...); } catch (e) { }` silently discards a malformed URI parameter and continues with the raw string. Downstream OData filter builds `PurchaseContract eq '<raw>'` and may hit an invalid filter.
findings.severityRationale: Minor robustness issue; low likelihood but opaque when it fires.
findings.recommendation: Log the decode failure with `Log.warning` and either reject the navigation or fall back to the raw string explicitly.

findings.title: Resource bundle key concatenated with runtime value
findings.issue: `MessageToast.show(oBundle.getText("parentResidualValue = ") + fResidual);` passes a key that includes `' = '` and spaces — the lookup will fail and show the raw placeholder.
findings.severityRationale: Mild UX glitch, visible to end users.
findings.recommendation: Use key `parentResidualValue` with a parameter placeholder: `oBundle.getText('parentResidualValue', [fResidual])` and define the key as `parent ResidualValue = {0}`.

findings.title: Duplicate `attachEventOnce('updateFinished', ...)` runs the residual calculation twice
findings.issue: `_filterChildContracts` attaches TWO `updateFinished` handlers back-to-back, both of which call `_calculateParentResidual`. Each table refresh runs the parent read twice.
findings.severityRationale: Wasted OData call per refresh and potential double toast message.
findings.recommendation: Keep a single `attachEventOnce` handler that performs both steps (`_calculateParentResidual` then `_fetchPlantsForChildren`).

findings.title: Dynamic `sap.ui.core.format.NumberFormat` lookup in formatter
findings.issue: `formatItalianNumber` references `sap.ui.core.format.NumberFormat` through the global tree. This module is not listed in `sap.ui.define`, so it is loaded on demand through the deprecated sync lookup.
findings.severityRationale: Minor module-loading issue; same in `childcontractList.controller.js`.
findings.recommendation: Add `"sap/ui/core/format/NumberFormat"` to the `sap.ui.define` dependencies and reference `NumberFormat.getFloatInstance(...)` directly.

findings.title: No OPA/QUnit test files present under `webapp/test`
findings.issue: `package.json` declares `unit-test` and `int-test` scripts, but no `webapp/test/unit` or `webapp/test/integration` directory exists in the upload. The lock/edit/create flow is complex and ships without regression coverage.
findings.severityRationale: Universal hygiene — missing tests for a transactional UI is a maintenance risk.
findings.recommendation: Add QUnit tests for `formatItalianNumber`, `_parseItalianNumber`, `_calculateParentResidual`, and OPA journeys for the create-child dialog, edit-save flow, and lock contention path.

summary.assessment: Blockers present — CSRF disabled on OData routes, missing authorization scopes, controller lifecycle leaks and broken concurrency UI require remediation before go-live
